title: Historical simulation VaR and ES, single asset, linear quantile
deliverables: summary json: var, es (positive decimals) per level
frame: DIKETAHUI: returns r [T] (decimal) of one asset, confidence c (e.g. 0.95, 0.99). DITANYAKAN: 1-day VaR_c and ES_c as positive return fractions. RUMUS: card Core 1-2; q = np.quantile(r, 1-c) (linear, type 7); VaR = -q; ES = -mean(r[r <= q]); toolkit historical_var_es(r, level=c, method='linear'). JAWAB: 1) clean r (drop NaN), keep time order irrelevant. 2) q at tail prob 1-c. 3) VaR=-q. 4) ES = -mean of returns <= q. 5) check ES >= VaR > 0.
pitfalls: reporting negative quantile as VaR
np.percentile scale 0-100 vs np.quantile 0-1

title: HS VaR as order statistic (k-th worst loss, Jorion/Basel)
deliverables: summary json: var, es, k index used
frame: DIKETAHUI: returns r [n], confidence c; text says 'k-th worst', 'order statistic' or 'no interpolation'. DITANYAKAN: VaR_c as the k-th largest loss; ES as mean of the k worst (or losses >= VaR). RUMUS: card Core 2 + Conventions: L = -r sorted descending; k = ceil(n(1-c)); VaR = L_(k) = sorted[k-1]; ES = mean(L_(1..k)); toolkit historical_var_es(method='lower' or order-statistic option). JAWAB: 1) L=-r. 2) sort descending. 3) k=ceil(n(1-c)) (guard float: round n(1-c) to 1e-9 before ceil). 4) VaR=L[k-1]. 5) ES=mean(L[:k]). 6) verify VaR equals an observed loss.
pitfalls: floating n(1-c) like 2.5000000001 gives wrong ceil
mixing order statistic with np.quantile interpolation

title: HS VaR with inverted-CDF quantile (smallest x with F(x) >= p)
frame: DIKETAHUI: returns r [n], c; text defines VaR via empirical distribution 'smallest x with F(x) >= 1-c' (returns) or F_L(x) >= c (losses). DITANYAKAN: VaR, ES consistent with that quantile definition. RUMUS: card Conventions; q = np.quantile(r, 1-c, method='inverted_cdf'); or on losses np.quantile(-r, c, method='inverted_cdf'); ES = -mean(r[r <= q]). JAWAB: 1) pick whether the definition is on returns or losses (they differ by one order statistic at ties of n(1-c)). 2) compute q. 3) VaR=-q. 4) ES over r <= q. 5) report the method used.
pitfalls: losses-side and returns-side inverted CDF are not mirror images when n(1-c) is an integer

title: HS expected shortfall with strict tail or Acerbi-Tasche fractional tail
deliverables: summary json: var, es_geq, es_strict, es_fractional
frame: DIKETAHUI: returns r [n], c. DITANYAKAN: ES under the stated tail convention (>= VaR, > VaR, or fractional). RUMUS: card Core 1, V3: ES_geq = mean(L[L >= VaR]); ES_strict = mean(L[L > VaR]); Acerbi-Tasche: k=floor(n(1-c)), ES = [sum_{j<=k} L_(j) + (n(1-c)-k) L_(k+1)]/(n(1-c)) with L descending; toolkit historical_var_es(es_tail='geq'|'gt'). JAWAB: 1) L=-r sorted descending. 2) VaR by the stated quantile. 3) apply tail rule. 4) check ES >= VaR; fractional ES lies between adjacent tail means.
formulas: ES_AT = (1/(n alpha)) [sum_{j=1..k} L_(j) + (n alpha - k) L_(k+1)], alpha = 1-c
pitfalls: strict tail can be empty when VaR equals the worst loss

title: Dollar VaR and ES from a price series and notional
deliverables: summary json: var_pct, es_pct, var_usd, es_usd
frame: DIKETAHUI: prices P [T+1] (sorted by date), notional or position value V, c. DITANYAKAN: VaR and ES in currency (and as fraction). RUMUS: card Core 1-2, Conventions: r = P_t/P_{t-1} - 1 (or log); VaR_frac by HS; VaR_$ = V * VaR_frac; for log returns exact loss V(1-e^{q}) only if asked; toolkit historical_var_es(..., value=V). JAWAB: 1) sort ascending by date. 2) returns [T]. 3) HS VaR, ES fraction. 4) multiply by V. 5) check currency ES >= VaR.
pitfalls: using latest price instead of position value as notional

title: VaR and ES table across several confidence levels and methods
frame: DIKETAHUI: returns r [T], levels [C], list of methods [M]. DITANYAKAN: one row per (method, level): VaR, ES positive. RUMUS: card Core 2-4, 10; toolkit historical_var_es, parametric_var_es(dist='normal'|'t'), cornish_fisher_var. JAWAB: 1) fit parameters once (mu, sigma ddof=1; t df/loc/scale). 2) loop levels and methods. 3) assemble long table [M*C]. 4) checks: ES >= VaR per row; VaR increasing in level within method.
pitfalls: alpha=0.01 written as level: convert tail prob to c = 1-alpha

title: Portfolio HS VaR from multi-asset prices and fixed weights
frame: DIKETAHUI: prices [T+1 x N] (wide, or long to pivot), weights w [N] (sum 1), c, notional. DITANYAKAN: portfolio VaR, ES (fraction and currency). RUMUS: card Core 1-2, V1(a): R = pct_change [T x N]; r_p = R w; HS on r_p; toolkit portfolio_returns(prices, w, kind='simple'), var_from_portfolio. JAWAB: 1) pivot long data, inner-join dates, order columns to match w. 2) simple returns. 3) r_p = R @ w. 4) HS VaR/ES. 5) times notional. 6) check sum w = 1.
pitfalls: weights matched to wrong column order
forward-filled prices producing zero returns

title: Portfolio VaR on averaged log returns (kind log_avg)
frame: DIKETAHUI: prices [T+1 x N], weights w [N]; text says portfolio return is the weighted average of asset log returns. DITANYAKAN: VaR, ES of that series. RUMUS: card V1(b): r_i = ln(P_t/P_{t-1}); r_p = sum w_i r_i; HS; toolkit portfolio_returns(kind='log_avg'). JAWAB: 1) log returns [T x N]. 2) weighted sum [T]. 3) quantile and tail mean. 4) dollar = notional * (-q) unless exact loss requested.
pitfalls: this is not the log of the portfolio gross return - do exactly what the text says

title: Portfolio VaR on log of portfolio gross return (kind log_portfolio)
frame: DIKETAHUI: prices [T+1 x N], weights w [N]; text defines r_p = ln(sum w_i P_i,t/P_i,t-1). DITANYAKAN: VaR, ES on that series. RUMUS: card V1(c): r_p = ln(sum_i w_i exp(l_i)) with l_i asset log returns; toolkit portfolio_returns(kind='log_portfolio'). JAWAB: 1) asset gross returns. 2) weighted sum, log. 3) HS. 4) compare to log_avg if both asked (log_portfolio >= log_avg by Jensen).

title: HS VaR on current holdings: P&L scenarios from historical returns
frame: DIKETAHUI: shares n [N], current prices P_T [N], historical returns R [T x N]. DITANYAKAN: VaR, ES in currency of today's book. RUMUS: card backtesting Core 8 / Core 2: position x_i = n_i P_i,T; scenario P&L_s = sum_i x_i R_s,i (linear) or full reval sum n_i (P_i,T(1+R_s,i) - P_i,T); VaR = -Q_{1-c}(P&L). JAWAB: 1) x = n * P_T. 2) P&L [T] = R @ x. 3) quantile of P&L at 1-c, negate. 4) ES = -mean(P&L <= q). 5) check vs weight-based VaR times total value.
pitfalls: using historical position values instead of current ones

title: 10-day HS VaR from overlapping h-day returns
frame: DIKETAHUI: daily log returns r [T], horizon h, c. DITANYAKAN: h-day VaR (and ES) from overlapping sums. RUMUS: card Core 9, V5(b): R_h = r.rolling(h).sum().dropna() -> [T-h+1]; VaR_h = -Q_{1-c}(R_h); simple returns: prod(1+r)-1 over each window; toolkit scale_horizon(method='overlapping') if provided. JAWAB: 1) sort ascending. 2) rolling h-sum (log) or rolling compound (simple). 3) count T-h+1. 4) quantile, ES. 5) optionally compare with sqrt(h) VaR_1.
pitfalls: applying sqrt(h) when overlapping sums were requested

title: 10-day HS VaR from non-overlapping blocks
frame: DIKETAHUI: daily returns r [T], h, c; text says non-overlapping. DITANYAKAN: h-day VaR from floor(T/h) block returns. RUMUS: card V5(c): blocks r[k h:(k+1) h] for k = 0..floor(T/h)-1 (start from oldest unless told to anchor at newest); log: sum; simple: prod(1+r)-1; HS on blocks. JAWAB: 1) decide anchor (oldest or newest end) per text. 2) form blocks, drop remainder. 3) quantile of block returns. 4) report n_blocks.
pitfalls: remainder block of fewer than h days included

title: Square-root-of-time scaling of parametric VaR with and without drift
frame: DIKETAHUI: 1-day mu, sigma (or VaR_1), horizon h, c. DITANYAKAN: h-day VaR. RUMUS: card Core 9: zero drift VaR_h = sqrt(h) VaR_1; with drift VaR_h = z_c sigma sqrt(h) - h mu; toolkit scale_horizon(var_1d, h, method='sqrt', mu=mu). JAWAB: 1) z_c = norm.ppf(c). 2) choose with/without drift per text. 3) compute. 4) check ratio sqrt(h) in the zero-drift case.
formulas: VaR_h = z sigma sqrt(h) - h mu
pitfalls: scaling a VaR that already contains -mu by sqrt(h) (drift must scale by h)

title: Normal (variance-covariance) VaR and ES with sample mean
deliverables: summary json: mu, sigma, var, es
frame: DIKETAHUI: returns r [T], c. DITANYAKAN: normal VaR and ES (positive fractions). RUMUS: card Core 3, V4(a), V6(a): mu = mean, sigma = std ddof=1; VaR = z_c sigma - mu; ES = sigma phi(z_c)/(1-c) - mu; toolkit parametric_var_es(r, level=c, dist='normal'). JAWAB: 1) mu, sigma. 2) z_c = norm.ppf(c) exactly. 3) VaR, ES. 4) ES/VaR > 1 check.
pitfalls: using rounded 2.33 or 1.645 literals

title: Zero-mean normal VaR (RiskMetrics convention)
frame: DIKETAHUI: returns r [T] or sigma, c; text says zero mean or RiskMetrics. DITANYAKAN: VaR = z sigma, ES = sigma phi(z)/(1-c). RUMUS: card V4(b): sigma = sqrt(mean(r^2)) if zero-mean variance is implied, else std; VaR = z_c sigma; ES = sigma phi(z_c)/(1-c); toolkit parametric_var_es(mu=0, sigma=...). JAWAB: 1) decide sigma estimator (zero-mean second moment vs std). 2) VaR, ES. 3) times notional.
pitfalls: subtracting the sample mean when the text imposes mu = 0

title: Normal VaR from MLE (ddof=0) versus sample standard deviation
deliverables: summary json: sigma_mle, sigma_sample, var_mle, var_sample
frame: DIKETAHUI: returns r [T], c; text says 'MLE' or 'fit a normal'. DITANYAKAN: VaR (and ES) under the stated estimator. RUMUS: card V6: sigma_mle = sqrt(mean((r-mean)^2)) (ddof=0, scipy norm.fit); sigma_s = ddof=1; ratio sqrt((T-1)/T). JAWAB: 1) choose estimator from the text word. 2) VaR = z sigma - mu. 3) if both asked, report both.

title: Parametric VaR from given scalar moments (no data)
frame: DIKETAHUI: position V, annual mu_a, sigma_a, horizon in days h, trading days per year D, c. DITANYAKAN: VaR and ES in currency over h days. RUMUS: card Core 3, 9: mu_h = mu_a h/D; sigma_h = sigma_a sqrt(h/D); VaR = V(z sigma_h - mu_h); ES = V(sigma_h phi(z)/(1-c) - mu_h). JAWAB: 1) convert annual to horizon (variance scales linearly). 2) z = norm.ppf(c). 3) VaR, ES in currency. 4) drop mu if text says ignore drift.
pitfalls: scaling sigma by h/D instead of sqrt(h/D)

title: ES at 97.5% versus VaR at 99% (FRTB calibration)
frame: DIKETAHUI: returns r [T] or sigma, mu. DITANYAKAN: ES_0.975 and VaR_0.99 under normal (and HS) and their ratio. RUMUS: card Completing: normal ES_0.975 = sigma phi(z_0.975)/0.025 - mu, VaR_0.99 = z_0.99 sigma - mu (close under normality); HS versions by Core 2. JAWAB: 1) compute both normal measures. 2) compute HS ones. 3) ratio ES/VaR; fat tails raise HS ES_0.975 above VaR_0.99.

title: Student-t VaR and ES from loc-scale MLE fit
deliverables: summary json: nu, loc, scale, var, es
frame: DIKETAHUI: returns r [T], c. DITANYAKAN: fitted (nu, loc, scale), VaR and ES. RUMUS: card Core 4: (nu, loc, scale) = scipy.stats.t.fit(r); q = t.ppf(c, nu); VaR = scale q - loc; ES = scale f_nu(q)/(1-c) (nu+q^2)/(nu-1) - loc; toolkit var_es_student_t(loc, scale, nu, c) / parametric_var_es(dist='t'). JAWAB: 1) fit t. 2) q. 3) VaR, ES. 4) check nu > 1 for ES finite. 5) compare with normal.
pitfalls: omitting (nu+q^2)/(nu-1)
using sigma as scale without sqrt((nu-2)/nu)

title: Student-t VaR with unit-variance scaling at given nu and sigma
frame: DIKETAHUI: mu, sigma (std of returns), nu > 2, c. DITANYAKAN: t VaR and ES matching variance sigma^2. RUMUS: card Core 4: scale = sigma sqrt((nu-2)/nu); then loc-scale formulas with loc = mu. JAWAB: 1) scale. 2) q = t.ppf(c, nu). 3) VaR = scale q - mu. 4) ES. 5) note at 95% t VaR may be below normal VaR.
pitfalls: plugging sigma directly as t scale

title: Student-t degrees of freedom by method of moments from kurtosis
deliverables: summary json: excess_kurtosis, nu, var, es
frame: DIKETAHUI: returns r [T], c; df not given and MLE not requested. DITANYAKAN: nu, t VaR, ES. RUMUS: card Completing: K = excess kurtosis (scipy kurtosis fisher=True, bias per text); nu = 4 + 6/K (K>0); scale = sigma sqrt((nu-2)/nu); Core 4. JAWAB: 1) K. 2) nu. 3) scale. 4) VaR, ES. 5) if K <= 0 fall back to normal and say so.
pitfalls: Pearson kurtosis (normal = 3) used where excess kurtosis is required

title: Normal versus Student-t VaR crossing across confidence levels
frame: DIKETAHUI: sigma, mu, nu, levels [C]. DITANYAKAN: VaR under normal and variance-matched t per level. RUMUS: card Invariants: t VaR exceeds normal at high c, may be smaller at 95%; Core 3-4. JAWAB: 1) unit-variance t scale. 2) VaR per level for both. 3) report sign of difference per level; do not 'fix' the crossing.

title: Cornish-Fisher modified VaR from sample skewness and kurtosis
deliverables: summary json: skew, ex_kurt, z_cf, var_cf, var_normal
frame: DIKETAHUI: returns r [T], c. DITANYAKAN: Cornish-Fisher VaR (and normal VaR for comparison). RUMUS: card Core 10: z = norm.ppf(1-c) (negative); z_cf = z + (z^2-1)S/6 + (z^3-3z)K/24 - (2z^3-5z)S^2/36; VaR = -(mu + z_cf sigma); toolkit cornish_fisher_var(mu, sigma, skew, excess_kurt, level=c). JAWAB: 1) mu, sigma ddof=1, S, K (excess) of returns. 2) z_cf. 3) VaR. 4) compare with normal; negative skew raises VaR.
pitfalls: using z = +2.326 (loss side) in the expansion flips the skew term
moments of losses instead of returns

title: Cornish-Fisher ES (modified ES) via integration of the adjusted quantile
frame: DIKETAHUI: returns r [T] (or mu, sigma, S, K), c. DITANYAKAN: Cornish-Fisher ES. RUMUS: card Core 1, 10: ES_c = (1/(1-c)) int_c^1 VaR_cf(u) du; evaluate on a fine grid of u in (c,1) (midpoints) or quad. JAWAB: 1) VaR_cf(u) function. 2) integrate numerically. 3) check ES >= VaR; note CF quantile may be non-monotone for large |S|, K - report.

title: Age-weighted (BRW) historical VaR, first cumulative weight >= 1-c
frame: DIKETAHUI: returns r [n] oldest -> newest, lambda, c. DITANYAKAN: BRW VaR and ES. RUMUS: card Core 5: w_i = lambda^{n-i}(1-lambda)/(1-lambda^n), i=1 oldest; sort (r, w) ascending by r; cum w; VaR = -r at first index with cum >= 1-c; ES = -sum(w r)/sum(w) over that tail; toolkit age_weighted_var_es(r, lam, level=c, interpolate=False). JAWAB: 1) weights in time order (newest largest). 2) sort pairs. 3) cumsum. 4) VaR. 5) ES. 6) check sum w = 1.
pitfalls: weights not re-sorted with returns
newest given smallest weight

title: BRW VaR with interpolation between cumulative weights
frame: DIKETAHUI: returns r [n], lambda, c; text asks for interpolated weighted quantile. DITANYAKAN: interpolated BRW VaR. RUMUS: card Core 5 + Pitfalls: after sorting, find k with cum_{k-1} < 1-c <= cum_k; interpolate r linearly between r_(k-1), r_(k) on cumulative weight (or mid-point cum - w/2, as stated); toolkit age_weighted_var_es(interpolate=True). JAWAB: 1) weights, sort, cumsum. 2) bracket 1-c. 3) linear interpolation. 4) VaR=-q. 5) report step version too.
pitfalls: interpolating when the text says first cumulative weight >= 1-c

title: BRW lambda sensitivity table
deliverables: table rows (lambda, var, es, effective n)
frame: DIKETAHUI: returns r [n], lambdas [K], c. DITANYAKAN: BRW VaR/ES per lambda and the equal-weight HS reference. RUMUS: card Core 5, Invariants: lambda -> 1 reproduces un-interpolated HS; effective sample 1/sum w^2. JAWAB: 1) per lambda weights, VaR, ES. 2) n_eff = 1/sum w^2. 3) append HS (order statistic) row. 4) check monotone behaviour is not assumed.

title: Filtered historical simulation, single asset with EWMA volatility
frame: DIKETAHUI: returns r [T], lambda, seed rule, c. DITANYAKAN: FHS VaR and ES for T+1. RUMUS: card Core 6: sigma_t from EWMA using data through t-1; z_t = r_t/sigma_t; sigma_{T+1} uses r_T; scenarios r* = z sigma_{T+1}; HS on r*; toolkit filtered_hs_var_es(r, lam, level=c, init=...). JAWAB: 1) EWMA sigma series [T] (forecast form). 2) z [T]. 3) sigma_{T+1}. 4) scenarios. 5) quantile, ES. 6) check scenario std approx sigma_{T+1}.
pitfalls: using sigma_t that already includes r_t (look-ahead) to standardise r_t

title: Filtered HS with GARCH(1,1) volatility
deliverables: summary json: garch params, sigma_next, var, es
frame: DIKETAHUI: returns r [T], c; GARCH params given or to be fitted. DITANYAKAN: FHS VaR, ES using GARCH sigma. RUMUS: card Core 6 + volatility-models Core 2: fit GARCH (toolkit fit_garch11 or arch with percent scaling); z = (r - mu)/sigma_t; sigma_{T+1}^2 = omega + alpha e_T^2 + beta sigma_T^2; r* = mu + z sigma_{T+1}. JAWAB: 1) fit / filter. 2) z. 3) one-step forecast. 4) scenarios. 5) HS VaR, ES.
formulas: sigma2_{T+1} = omega + alpha e_T^2 + beta sigma2_T
pitfalls: using in-sample sigma_T instead of forecast sigma_{T+1}

title: Multi-asset filtered HS with row resampling
frame: DIKETAHUI: returns [T x N], weights w [N], per-asset vol model, c. DITANYAKAN: portfolio FHS VaR, ES. RUMUS: card Core 6: Z [T x N] = R/Sigma_t per column; scenario s uses whole row z_s scaled by sigma_{i,T+1}; r*_p,s = sum w_i z_s,i sigma_i,T+1; do NOT apply Cholesky of R in addition. JAWAB: 1) per-asset sigma series and next-day sigma. 2) Z rows. 3) scenarios [T x N] (or bootstrap rows with seed). 4) portfolio scenario returns. 5) VaR, ES.
pitfalls: resampling columns independently destroys correlation

title: FHS multi-day horizon by bootstrapped GARCH paths
frame: DIKETAHUI: returns r [T], fitted GARCH params, horizon h, n_paths, seed, c. DITANYAKAN: h-day VaR/ES from simulated cumulative returns. RUMUS: card Core 6, 8: per path draw z* from standardized residuals (rng.choice with seed), update sigma2_{t+1} = omega + alpha (sigma_t z*)^2 + beta sigma2_t, accumulate r; VaR on [n_paths] cumulative returns. JAWAB: 1) residual pool. 2) loop h steps vectorised over paths. 3) cumulative log returns. 4) quantile, ES. 5) report generator used.
formulas: sigma2_{t+1} = omega + alpha e_t^2 + beta sigma2_t
pitfalls: legacy np.random vs default_rng mismatch when a seed is pinned

title: EWMA (RiskMetrics) one-day VaR for a single asset
frame: DIKETAHUI: returns r [T], lambda, seed rule, c, notional. DITANYAKAN: VaR for T+1 under normal zero mean. RUMUS: card Core 3 + volatility-models Core 1: s2_{t+1} = lambda s2_t + (1-lambda) r_t^2; VaR = z_c sigma_{T+1}; toolkit ewma_var_es(r, lam, level=c), ewma_vol. JAWAB: 1) seed per text (first squared return or initial sample variance). 2) recurse through r_T. 3) VaR, ES. 4) currency.
pitfalls: stopping recursion at T-1 for a 'current' VaR

title: Delta-normal portfolio VaR from covariance matrix and weights
frame: DIKETAHUI: weights or currency positions w [N], covariance Sigma [N x N] (or vols [N] and correlation [N x N]), c. DITANYAKAN: portfolio VaR, ES. RUMUS: card Core 7: Sigma = D C D if vols and correlations given; sigma_p = sqrt(w' Sigma w); VaR = z_c sigma_p (minus w'mu if mean included); ES = phi(z_c)/(1-c) sigma_p; toolkit component_var(w, cov, level=c, value=V). JAWAB: 1) build Sigma, check symmetric PSD. 2) sigma_p. 3) VaR, ES. 4) currency if w in currency.
pitfalls: mixing daily and annual covariance

title: Diversification benefit: undiversified versus diversified VaR
deliverables: summary json: individual var [N], undiversified, diversified, benefit
frame: DIKETAHUI: positions x [N] (currency), vols [N], correlation [N x N], c. DITANYAKAN: individual VaRs, their sum, portfolio VaR, benefit. RUMUS: card Core 7: VaR_i = z |x_i| s_i; undiversified = sum VaR_i (rho = 1); diversified = z sqrt(x' Sigma x); benefit = undiversified - diversified. JAWAB: 1) Sigma. 2) VaR_i. 3) sum. 4) portfolio VaR. 5) benefit >= 0 for long-only.

title: Marginal VaR per asset (delta-normal)
frame: DIKETAHUI: positions w [N] (currency or weights), Sigma [N x N], c. DITANYAKAN: marginal VaR dVaR/dw_i [N]. RUMUS: card Core 7: MVaR_i = z (Sigma w)_i/sigma_p; beta form MVaR_i = beta_i VaR/W with beta_i = (Sigma w)_i/sigma_p^2 when w in currency and W = total value. JAWAB: 1) Sigma w. 2) sigma_p. 3) MVaR. 4) finite-difference check (VaR(w + h e_i) - VaR(w))/h.
pitfalls: multiplying by sigma_p instead of dividing

title: Component VaR and percent contributions (Euler allocation)
deliverables: per-asset table: weight, marginal_var, component_var, pct
frame: DIKETAHUI: w [N], Sigma [N x N], c, portfolio value V. DITANYAKAN: component VaR [N] in currency and pct; total VaR. RUMUS: card Core 7: CVaR_i = w_i MVaR_i = z w_i (Sigma w)_i/sigma_p; pct_i = CVaR_i/VaR; sum CVaR = VaR; toolkit component_var(w, cov, level=c, value=V). JAWAB: 1) sigma_p, VaR. 2) MVaR. 3) CVaR, pct. 4) check sum equals VaR to 1e-10; negative components allowed (hedges).

title: Incremental VaR of a new position: exact versus marginal approximation
deliverables: summary json: var_before, var_after, ivar_exact, ivar_approx
frame: DIKETAHUI: current positions w [N], trade a [N], Sigma, c. DITANYAKAN: incremental VaR exact and first-order. RUMUS: card Core 7: IVaR = VaR(w+a) - VaR(w); approx a' MVaR(w). JAWAB: 1) VaR(w). 2) VaR(w+a). 3) difference. 4) a' MVaR. 5) note approximation error grows with trade size.

title: Component expected shortfall under normality
frame: DIKETAHUI: w [N], Sigma, c. DITANYAKAN: component ES [N] summing to ES. RUMUS: card Core 7 ES version: replace z by phi(z_c)/(1-c); CES_i = w_i (phi(z)/(1-c)) (Sigma w)_i/sigma_p; toolkit component_var(..., measure='es'). JAWAB: 1) sigma_p. 2) ES. 3) components. 4) check sum.

title: Historical-simulation component VaR and ES (conditional expectations)
frame: DIKETAHUI: returns R [T x N], weights w [N], c. DITANYAKAN: HS component ES (and VaR) per asset. RUMUS: card Core 7 (Euler) applied to simulation: CES_i = -w_i mean(R_s,i over tail scenarios s with L_p,s >= VaR); CVaR_i = -w_i R_s*,i at the VaR scenario (or average of a small kernel window, as stated). JAWAB: 1) r_p = R w. 2) VaR, tail set. 3) average asset returns over tail. 4) multiply by -w_i. 5) check sums equal ES and VaR.
pitfalls: single-scenario component VaR is noisy; follow the text's smoothing

title: Monte Carlo VaR with multivariate normal returns and Cholesky
frame: DIKETAHUI: mu [N], Sigma [N x N], weights or positions [N], n_sims, seed, c. DITANYAKAN: MC VaR and ES. RUMUS: card Core 8: L = cholesky(Sigma) (lower); Z [n x N] ~ N(0,1) via np.random.default_rng(seed).standard_normal; R = mu + Z L'; P&L = R w; HS estimator on P&L. JAWAB: 1) Cholesky. 2) draws in stated order. 3) portfolio returns. 4) quantile, ES. 5) compare with analytic delta-normal.
pitfalls: Z L instead of Z L' (wrong covariance)
generator stream mismatch

title: Monte Carlo VaR with full revaluation of an option position
frame: DIKETAHUI: spot S, option terms (K, T, r, q, sigma), position size, horizon h days, return vol, n_sims, seed, c. DITANYAKAN: VaR, ES of position value change over h. RUMUS: card Core 8: simulate S_h = S exp((mu - s^2/2) dt + s sqrt(dt) Z); reprice with remaining maturity T - h/D (BS); P&L = n (V(S_h) - V(S)); HS on P&L. JAWAB: 1) base value. 2) simulate spot. 3) revalue each scenario (vectorised BS). 4) P&L. 5) VaR, ES.
formulas: PnL = n [V(S_h, T - dt) - V(S, T)]
pitfalls: forgetting to reduce time to maturity at horizon

title: Delta-gamma VaR versus full revaluation
frame: DIKETAHUI: S, option greeks delta, gamma (or BS inputs), position, horizon vol, c, n_sims, seed. DITANYAKAN: VaR under delta-normal, delta-gamma MC and full reval. RUMUS: card Core 7-8: dS = S r; dV ~ delta dS + 0.5 gamma dS^2; delta-normal VaR = z |delta| S sigma; simulate r to get delta-gamma and full P&L. JAWAB: 1) greeks. 2) delta VaR. 3) simulate returns. 4) quadratic P&L, full P&L. 5) quantiles and comparison.

title: Delta-gamma VaR by Cornish-Fisher on P&L moments
deliverables: summary json: mean, var, skew, var_cf
frame: DIKETAHUI: delta, gamma, S, sigma (horizon), c. DITANYAKAN: analytic delta-gamma VaR via moment matching. RUMUS: card Core 10 on P&L dV = delta S x + 0.5 gamma S^2 x^2, x ~ N(0, s^2): E = 0.5 gamma S^2 s^2; Var = delta^2 S^2 s^2 + 0.5 gamma^2 S^4 s^4; third central moment = 3 delta^2 gamma S^4 s^4 + gamma^3 S^6 s^6. JAWAB: 1) moments, skew. 2) CF quantile of P&L at 1-c. 3) VaR = -quantile. 4) optionally verify by MC.
formulas: mu3 = 3 delta^2 gamma S^4 s^4 + gamma^3 S^6 s^6

title: Sampling error of a VaR estimate: order-statistic or bootstrap confidence interval
frame: DIKETAHUI: returns r [n], c, interval level g, n_boot, seed. DITANYAKAN: VaR with a confidence interval. RUMUS: card Core 2 + Jorion: distribution-free CI from order statistics: ranks j with Binomial(n, 1-c) bounds; or bootstrap: resample r with replacement B times, VaR_b, percentile CI; asymptotic SE = sqrt(p(1-p)/n)/f(q). JAWAB: 1) point VaR. 2) chosen CI method. 3) report bounds as positive losses (upper bound of loss is lower return).

title: Monte Carlo VaR standard error and convergence table
frame: DIKETAHUI: distribution of P&L to simulate, list of n_sims [K], seed, c. DITANYAKAN: VaR estimates by sample size and their standard errors. RUMUS: card Core 8 + order-statistic SE: SE ~ sqrt(p(1-p)/n)/f(q) with f by KDE, or repeat with independent seeds and take std. JAWAB: 1) simulate largest n once, take prefixes (or independent runs as stated). 2) VaR per n. 3) SE. 4) check SE decays like 1/sqrt(n).

title: Kernel density VaR and ES (Gaussian kernel, Silverman bandwidth)
frame: DIKETAHUI: returns r [n], c. DITANYAKAN: KDE VaR and ES. RUMUS: card Core 11: h = 0.9 min(sd, IQR/1.34) n^{-1/5} (Silverman) or scipy gaussian_kde default (Scott) as stated; F(x) = mean Phi((x - r_i)/h); solve F(q) = 1-c on a fine grid or brentq; ES via int x f(x) dx/(1-c); toolkit kernel_var_es(r, level=c). JAWAB: 1) bandwidth. 2) CDF on grid (range +- several sd). 3) quantile by interp. 4) ES integral (closed form per kernel: mean over i of r_i Phi(a_i) - h phi(a_i), a_i = (q - r_i)/h). 5) VaR=-q.
pitfalls: scipy gaussian_kde uses Scott's rule unless bw_method='silverman'

title: EVT peaks-over-threshold VaR and ES with GPD
deliverables: summary json: u, n_u, xi, beta, var, es
frame: DIKETAHUI: losses L [n] (= -r), threshold u (or quantile of L), c. DITANYAKAN: GPD parameters, VaR and ES. RUMUS: McNeil-Frey-Embrechts: fit GPD to excesses y = L - u, L > u (scipy genpareto.fit floc=0) -> xi, beta; VaR = u + (beta/xi)[((n/n_u)(1-c))^{-xi} - 1]; ES = VaR/(1-xi) + (beta - xi u)/(1-xi). JAWAB: 1) threshold. 2) excesses. 3) fit. 4) VaR, ES. 5) check xi < 1 for finite ES and c beyond threshold level.

title: Stressed VaR from a selected stress window
deliverables: summary json: stress window start, end, svar
frame: DIKETAHUI: returns r [T] with dates, window length W, c; stress period given or to be found. DITANYAKAN: stressed VaR (and the window used). RUMUS: Basel 2.5: VaR computed on the most severe W-day period; if not given, roll the window and pick the one maximising VaR; scale to 10 days by sqrt(10) if asked. JAWAB: 1) rolling HS VaR over all windows [T-W+1]. 2) argmax. 3) report dates ISO, sVaR. 4) horizon scaling.

title: Basel market-risk capital from VaR and stressed VaR
frame: DIKETAHUI: daily 10-day VaR series (last 60), sVaR series, multipliers m_c, m_s. DITANYAKAN: capital requirement. RUMUS: Basel 2.5: K = max(VaR_{t-1}, m_c avg60 VaR) + max(sVaR_{t-1}, m_s avg60 sVaR), m >= 3 (+ plus factor from backtesting). JAWAB: 1) last values. 2) 60-day means. 3) apply max terms. 4) sum.
formulas: K = max(VaR_{t-1}, m_c mean60 VaR) + max(sVaR_{t-1}, m_s mean60 sVaR)

title: ES subadditivity check versus VaR non-subadditivity
deliverables: summary json: var_p, sum_var_i, es_p, sum_es_i, flags
frame: DIKETAHUI: asset returns R [T x N] or loss scenarios, weights, c. DITANYAKAN: standalone and portfolio VaR and ES and subadditivity flags. RUMUS: card Invariants: ES(portfolio) <= sum ES_i (coherent, Artzner et al.); VaR may violate (e.g. independent defaultable bonds). JAWAB: 1) standalone measures (scaled by weights). 2) portfolio measures. 3) flags var_p <= sum, es_p <= sum. 4) report counterexample if VaR fails.

title: VaR of defaultable bonds (discrete loss distribution)
frame: DIKETAHUI: N independent bonds, PD p, loss per default LGD, c. DITANYAKAN: VaR and ES of single bond and portfolio. RUMUS: Hull RMFI: losses discrete; VaR = smallest loss l with P(L <= l) >= c; ES = E[L | tail] with fractional mass at the VaR atom (Acerbi-Tasche) or as stated; binomial counts for the portfolio. JAWAB: 1) loss pmf. 2) cdf. 3) VaR. 4) ES with atom splitting. 5) compare sum of standalone VaR.

title: Bond VaR via duration mapping (yield volatility)
frame: DIKETAHUI: bond price P (or position V), modified duration D (or DV01), yield change vol sigma_y (bp or decimal per day), c. DITANYAKAN: interest-rate VaR. RUMUS: Jorion: dV ~ -D V dy; sigma_V = D V sigma_y; VaR = z_c D V sigma_y; with convexity C: dV ~ -D V dy + 0.5 C V dy^2. JAWAB: 1) convert bp to decimal. 2) sigma_V. 3) VaR. 4) multi-bond: Sigma of key-rate changes and DV01 vector -> sqrt(x' Sigma x).
pitfalls: bp vs decimal yield changes

title: FX position VaR in domestic currency
frame: DIKETAHUI: foreign asset value V_f, exchange rate X (domestic per foreign), vols of asset and FX, correlation rho, c. DITANYAKAN: VaR of the position in domestic currency. RUMUS: Jorion mapping: domestic return ~ r_asset + r_fx; sigma^2 = s_a^2 + s_x^2 + 2 rho s_a s_x; VaR = z X V_f sigma; HS alternative: r_dom = (1+r_a)(1+r_x) - 1. JAWAB: 1) domestic value. 2) combined vol or HS series. 3) VaR. 4) decomposition into asset vs FX components if asked.
formulas: sigma_dom^2 = s_a^2 + s_x^2 + 2 rho s_a s_x
pitfalls: quote convention inverted (foreign per domestic)

title: Long-format price data pivoted and aligned for portfolio VaR
deliverables: summary json: n_dates, n_returns, var, es
frame: DIKETAHUI: rows (date, symbol, price) [n_raw], weights by symbol, c. DITANYAKAN: portfolio VaR, ES plus alignment counts. RUMUS: card Pitfalls: parse dates, pivot_table(index=date, columns=symbol, values=price, aggfunc='last') when duplicates, dropna(how='any') (inner join), sort ascending, reorder columns to weight keys, pct_change(fill_method=None). JAWAB: 1) pivot. 2) align. 3) returns [T x N]. 4) r_p. 5) HS / parametric. 6) report counts: aligned dates, returns = dates - 1.

title: Rolling-window VaR estimate series (reporting, not testing)
frame: DIKETAHUI: returns r [T] with dates, window W, method, c. DITANYAKAN: VaR series where VaR_t uses r[t-W..t-1] (forecast) or r[t-W+1..t] (estimate as of t), as stated. RUMUS: card Core 2-3 applied per window; out-of-sample alignment (see backtesting family Core 7). JAWAB: 1) decide alignment. 2) loop or rolling apply. 3) emit dated series. 4) count = T - W (forecast) or T - W + 1 (as-of).
pitfalls: off-by-one in count of windows

title: Multi-method VaR comparison with model choice summary
frame: DIKETAHUI: returns r [T], c, lambda. DITANYAKAN: VaR, ES for HS, normal, t, CF, EWMA, FHS; spread between methods. RUMUS: card Core 2-6, 10 with toolkit historical_var_es, parametric_var_es, cornish_fisher_var, ewma_var_es, filtered_hs_var_es. JAWAB: 1) common cleaned r. 2) each method. 3) table. 4) identify highest/lowest; comment on fat tails (t, CF, HS above normal at 99%).

title: EWMA covariance portfolio VaR (RiskMetrics multi-asset)
frame: DIKETAHUI: returns R [T x N], lambda, seed rule, positions w [N], c. DITANYAKAN: current EWMA covariance and portfolio VaR. RUMUS: volatility-models Core 1: S_t = lambda S_{t-1} + (1-lambda) r_t r_t' through r_T; sigma_p = sqrt(w' S_T w); VaR = z_c sigma_p. JAWAB: 1) seed. 2) recursion with np.outer. 3) PSD check. 4) VaR, component VaR via component_var(w, S_T, level=c).

title: VaR in currency for a short position or long-short book
frame: DIKETAHUI: positions x [N] (signed currency), returns R [T x N], c. DITANYAKAN: VaR, ES of the signed book. RUMUS: card Core 1: P&L = R x (signs included); loss = -P&L; for a single short, losses come from the RIGHT tail of asset returns: VaR = Q_c(r) * |x|. JAWAB: 1) P&L series. 2) quantile of P&L at 1-c. 3) negate. 4) check negative component VaR for hedges.
pitfalls: using left tail of the asset for a short

title: Linear factor-mapped VaR (beta mapping to index)
frame: DIKETAHUI: positions x [N], betas [N], index vol s_m, residual vols [N] (optional), c. DITANYAKAN: VaR from beta mapping (systematic only or with specific risk). RUMUS: Jorion mapping: beta_p = sum x_i beta_i; systematic sigma = |beta_p| s_m; total variance = beta_p^2 s_m^2 + sum x_i^2 s_ei^2; VaR = z sigma. JAWAB: 1) dollar beta. 2) systematic sigma. 3) add residual if asked. 4) VaR.
formulas: sigma_p^2 = (sum x_i beta_i)^2 s_m^2 + sum x_i^2 s_e,i^2
